response.consequence: The hypothesized over-grant does not occur on this path.
response.explanation: toggleResourcePermissionLevel removes `*.*` on its first line (`currentPermissions.filter((p) => p !== "*.*")`, line 72), before the resource branch runs. The non-`*` branch then removes the resource's own permissions. It adds `*.*` back only if hasAllPermissions is true, and that cannot happen after a downgrade. So lowering one resource to "none" or "read" while `*.*` is present does not leave `*.*` in the result.

other_findings.consequence: The editor showed every resource as "all", but after one downgrade every other resource drops to "none" in the saved role.
other_findings.explanation: getResourcePermissionLevel reports "all" for every resource whenever `*.*` is present, even if no individual permissions are listed. toggleResourcePermissionLevel drops `*.*` at line 72 but does not expand it into individual permissions. If a role is stored with only `*.*`, lowering one resource leaves only the other individual permissions, which is an empty list. I did not check whether such roles exist in the data.
other_findings.title: Downgrading one resource on a role that holds only `*.*` clears all other resources

response.consequence: Hosts can't confirm paid, requires-confirmation bookings from the list. Pending bookings with payment enabled and no payment rows get a confirm button that was previously hidden.
response.explanation: The old confirm condition was `(isPending && !paymentAppData.enabled) || (paymentAppData.enabled && !!price && booking.paid)`. The refactor passes `showPendingPayment = paymentAppData.enabled && booking.payment.length && !booking.paid` into the context, and getPendingActions uses `(isPending && !showPendingPayment) || (showPendingPayment && booking.paid)`. Because showPendingPayment already requires `!booking.paid`, the second clause is always false. For a pending booking with payment enabled and already paid, the old code showed "confirm". The new code does not, since showPendingPayment is false so the first clause fires only when isPending is true, and it can wrongly fire in other states. Also, a pending booking with payment enabled but no payment rows now shows confirm, where the old code did not.

response.consequence: After a save, or any other refetch that changes the data, the editor unmounts and remounts. The user sees a flash of empty content and loses in-progress form state, such as the active tab and unsaved edits. It also causes redundant network refetches.
response.explanation: The effect's cleanup invalidates and resets the atom event-type query. It was meant to run only on unmount or when `id` changed. The change added `eventTypeQueryData` to the dependency array, so the cleanup now also runs whenever the fetched data changes, for example after a save refetches the event type. `resetQueries` clears the cached data to undefined, and the component then hits `if (!eventTypeQueryData) return null`. That unmounts the whole `EventType` form, and the form remounts only once the refetch completes. I did not open the update mutation's code, so I am assuming it invalidates this query after a save.
response.title: Adding eventTypeQueryData to effect deps resets the query and unmounts the form on every data change

hypotheses.failure_mode: When a role has `*.*` and the user lowers a single resource to "none" or "read", toggleResourcePermissionLevel only filters permissions starting with `${resource}.`. The global `*.*` entry stays in newPermissions. getResourcePermissionLevel returns "all" for every resource whenever `*.*` is present, so the downgrade is ignored in the UI. A saved role could keep full wildcard access even though the admin tried to restrict it.
